what: The apply pass that created the one column the 2026-09-02 dry run had found missing. Run by the operator from a SharePoint page on 2026-09-03: a DRY_RUN pass first, then the same script with DRY_RUN = false. One column created, 102 already present, none failed. Read against the specification, the estate's column set is now complete in the tenant: 103 of 103, and all five index targets indexed.
runner: scripts/provision-sharepoint-fields.browser.js (generated from the specification; browser devtools console, operator session)

source.capture: The operator's browser console output, pasted verbatim into the session.
source.startedUtcWhyNull: The provisioner prints no timestamp of its own, and this capture is a paste rather than a saved console export, so it carries no filename epoch to derive one from — the 2026-08-31 record's startedUtc came from such a filename. The date is the session date, 2026-09-03. Nothing in this record depends on the time of day, and a time is not invented to fill the field.

runs.meaning: A re-read immediately before the apply, in the same session. It agrees with the 2026-09-02 dry run: 102 present, one to create. The estate had not changed between the two dates.

runs.consoleSays: + Attempts (Number) / Created: 1   Already present: 102   Failed: 0 / Estate complete: 103/103 columns present.
runs.meaning: The provisioner reads each declared field before it writes and creates only what is absent. `Already present: 102` is therefore 102 successful reads; `Created: 1` is one field-creation call SharePoint accepted; `+ Attempts (Number)` names it.
A third independent read of the five index targets, after 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-02. All five already indexed; nothing to set.

noVerifyRun.why: The operator ran DRY_RUN and then apply, in that order. The dry run is a pre-state read, not a verify: it reports what was missing before the write, not what exists after it. No pass was made after the create, so nothing here re-read the column back out of the tenant. `Estate complete: 103/103` is the script adding its own created and present counters against the specification total — arithmetic over one pass, not a second reading.
noVerifyRun.whatIsAlreadyEstablishedWithoutIt: That SharePoint accepted the create: createfieldasxml returned ok, which is the tenant's own answer, and Failed: 0. What is not established is the created column's settings, or that it survived anything subsequent.
noVerifyRun.howItCloses: Either a DRY_RUN pass of the same script, which would report 103 present and 0 to create; or — requiring no extra step — saving the patched Web - OTP Verify under register ITEM-38. Power Automate validates every item/<Column> parameter against the connector operation AT SAVE TIME and refuses the whole flow with WorkflowOperationParametersExtraParameter when the list lacks the column. The patched definition writes Attempts. A successful save is therefore a read of this column by the platform that would otherwise reject it.
noVerifyRun.doesNotBlock: register ITEM-39, whose resolution criterion is a run record accounting for the column and a provisionedBy naming it. Both hold. This is a strengthening, and it is recorded as outstanding rather than left to be inferred.

indexRun.addressing: Each target is addressed by list GUID, not title — 'Global Tracking Queue' and 'DGO DIGITAL OPS' each exist on two sites in this tenant, and only the NITDADGO-EAAACTIVITYTRACKING pair are the declared targets.
indexRun.ledgerDerivation: The operator's paste carried the summary line, not the five per-target lines. These rows are DERIVED, not transcribed, and the derivation is exact: the index pass walks the declared targets once each, and every target increments exactly one of indexed / alreadyIndexed / indexFailed. Five declared targets with indexed = 0, alreadyIndexed = 5 and failed = 0 admits one assignment — every declared target read back Indexed: true from the tenant. Nothing per-target is claimed beyond that. (The script's own ledger string for this outcome is 'present'; these records have said 'already indexed' since 2026-08-31 and keep to it.)
indexRun.verified: A third independent read of all five targets, after the 2026-08-31 apply-and-verify and the 2026-09-02 dry run. Three separate dates agree that all five are indexed. The provisioning half of register ITEM-23 is not in doubt; its remaining criterion is live traffic.

howStronglyThisIsEstablished.created: CONFIRMED. createField POSTs to /_api/web/lists(guid'…')/fields/createfieldasxml and throws on a non-ok response, so a row is counted 'created' only where SharePoint accepted the create and 'FAILED: <status> <message>' otherwise. The run reported Created: 1, Failed: 0, and one ledger row reading 'created'. The tenant, not the script, is the authority for that.
howStronglyThisIsEstablished.estateComplete: The line `Estate complete: 103/103 columns present.` is the script's own arithmetic — created + present against the specification total — not a re-read after the write. What was read is the 102; what was written is the one. No post-apply verify pass was made, so this record does not present one.
howStronglyThisIsEstablished.theSecondReading: It arrives with register ITEM-38 and needs no extra step from the operator. Power Automate validates every item/<Column> parameter against the connector operation AT SAVE TIME and refuses the whole flow with WorkflowOperationParametersExtraParameter if the list lacks the column. The patched Web - OTP Verify writes Attempts. If it saves, the column exists; if the column did not exist, it could not save. That is a stricter reading than a repeat dry run, and it is the very next action in the sequence.
howStronglyThisIsEstablished.notClaimed: That the column is of the intended precision, display format or default. The specification declares Number with no further constraint, and the run created a Number. Nothing here inspects the created column's settings.

consoleNoise.observation: The pasted capture carries about a hundred lines of SharePoint's own page chrome around the run: an ad-blocking notice, service-worker router and cache logs from spserviceworker.js, icon re-registration, iframe sandbox warnings, and a `TypeError: Failed to fetch` inside spserviceworker.js during a manifest sync.
consoleNoise.attribution: None of it originates in scripts/provision-sharepoint-fields.browser.js. The script's output is prefixed and counted, and it reported Failed: 0 across both phases.
consoleNoise.theFailedFetch: It is raised by SharePoint's service worker against its own manifest endpoint, not by the provisioner. A failed request inside the provisioner is caught per field and printed as a failure row in the ledger; the ledger has one row and it reads 'created'. The run is unaffected.

closes: ITEM-39 — OTP_Transactions.Attempts is provisioned, and portal-field-spec.json now names this record in its provisionedBy.
The dependency ITEM-38 declared on ITEM-39. The OTP verify patch can now be saved.
whatThisDoesNotClose: ITEM-38 — the patched definition has not been applied. This run makes the save possible; it does not make it.

ITEM-23 — the index requirement is now confirmed three times over, but its remaining criterion is live traffic: one assignment and one flag write against a known reference returning 200. Neither has been exercised.
ITEM-2 — no flow was called. This is SharePoint REST, not a Power Automate execution.
